summary:
MissionPulse — Your Health Companion Beyond Earth — is a web-based astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to support health awareness during long-duration space missions.

Astronauts can record daily health indicators such as heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, sleep, mood, and fatigue. Interactive charts and personal baseline comparisons help them understand changes over time.

The platform also provides educational guidance on preventive health practices, when to seek crew medical support, and how spaceflight hazards affect human health. These explanations are informed by NASA's Human Research Program and Canadian Space Agency resources.

MissionPulse includes secure personal accounts, health history, and a publicly accessible fictional demo that allows anyone to explore the system.

Our goal is to make astronaut health monitoring understandable, accessible, and useful for future missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. MissionPulse is an educational prototype, not a medical diagnostic system.
details:
MissionPulse — Project Details

Problem and Solution

Long-duration space missions expose astronauts to physical and psychological health risks, while distance from Earth can make medical support more challenging. MissionPulse addresses this problem through an accessible, research-informed health-monitoring platform.

How It Works

Astronauts can create personal accounts, enter daily health measurements, and review their health history. The application supports indicators including heart rate, blood pressure, blood glucose, oxygen saturation, body temperature, sleep, mood, hydration, exercise, and fatigue.

Interactive charts visualize changes over time. When sufficient historical measurements are available, the system provides personal baseline comparisons to help users understand their recorded patterns.

MissionPulse also includes educational explanations about spaceflight health risks, preventive health considerations, and situations that may warrant discussion with crew medical personnel. These are linked to NASA and Canadian Space Agency research.

A separate fictional Explore Demo allows judges and visitors to experience the application without registering.

Technology

  • Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS
  • Supabase for authentication and personal health-record storage
  • Recharts for interactive health visualizations
  • GitHub for source-code management
  • Vercel for web deployment

Creativity and Impact

MissionPulse brings personal health tracking, understandable visual analytics, and spaceflight-specific health education into one workflow. Its combination of personal baseline comparisons, beginner-friendly explanations, and a publicly accessible demonstration distinguishes it from a basic health-recording dashboard.

The project is designed as an educational prototype that could inform the development of future astronaut health-support tools for lunar and Mars missions.

Limitations

MissionPulse does not diagnose medical conditions, prescribe treatments, connect to medical devices, or replace qualified crew medical support. The public demo uses fictional health records.

Live Application: https://missionpulse.vercel.app
